# Analysis of The Effects of Daily Quizzes

## Histogram of Quiz Effectiveness Scores

This distribution plot examines how the class rates the effectiveness of the quizzes. This allows me to see if students feel like the quizzes are effective or not. With this, I can also analyze the shape of the distribution to see if responses are skewed one way or the other. Skewed left tells me the class for the most part thinks they are helpful, skewed right tells me the class for the most part thinks they aren't helpful, a uniform distribution tells me they don't have a great impact, and a normal distribution can vary depending on where the center of the distribution is, but it likely indicates they are moderately helpful or not helpful.

<img src="/Analysis/static/imgs/output2.png" alt="Scatterplot of Effectiveness vs Understanding" width="500"/>

## Scatterplot of Quiz Effectiveness vs Understanding

This scatter plot helps determine whether there is a strong correlation between how effective people think the quizzes are and their understanding of the class. I am particularly looking to see if high quiz effectiveness is associated with better understanding of the course material. This helps determine whether short quizzes after every class are useful to students. 

<img src="/Analysis/static/imgs/output3.png" alt="Box Plot of Pace vs Understanding" width="500"/>

## Box Plot Showing Relationship Between Pace and Understanding

This boxplot examines whether the way a student perceives the pace coincides with their understanding of the material. This helps determine whether students who feel the class is moving faster or slower also have differences in their understanding of the class. I use this to help me determine if my idea of having small quizzes after every class could help the perceived pace as well as the student's understanding of the material every day.

## Overall Conclusion

Based on the analysis, my proposal to add daily quizzes after class to reinforce concepts for struggling students seems to be supported, but could also be inconclusive. Much of the data shows a strong and clear relationship between how the class was structured and how the student felt about the class overall. In this histogram that analyzed the effectiveness of quizzes there was a significant left skew where many students thought the quizzes were highly effective(a 6 or 7). This showed me that students percieve quizzes as already being highly beneficial to their ability to grasp the material, and that having more small quizzes could greatly help struggling students. The boxplot examining pace vs understanding also supports my idea as it showed a negative correlation, meaning that as the pace of the course that the student perceived increased, the understanding decreased. This can be proven as students who thought the pace of the course was a 7, had a median understanding of about a 3, showing that a quicker pace meant less understanding. I believe that adding a daily quiz would help decrease the pace while also improving understanding because it would allow students everyday to review what we just learned and hopefully allow them to get a better grasp of the content. However, the scatter plot examining quiz effectivness and understanding showed inconclusive results. While there were many students who both understood the material and thought the quizzes were effective, there were also many who thought the quizzes were effective but did not understand the material at all. The results were way too scatterred and showed no clear correlation between how a student perceieved the effectiveness of quizzes and how well the student felt they understood the material. 

## Recommendation

I recommend transitioning to a daily quiz model. Although the class did have some assignments due after classes, they were not implemented enough on a regular basis to where I felt like they helped a lot. I believe that by providing low-stakes practice opportunities, the course can provide a baseline for students who are struggling by the current pace and content, allowing them to identify areas that they need help within 24 hours of the material being taught. To further refine the idea there could be a system implemented where after the student completes the quiz they can be suggested a video that helps explain the content further. Also, allowing multiple attempts on the quiz could decrease the stress of the graded aspect of the assignment for struggling students, as they can take the quiz many times until they feel they understand the content. 

## Potential Costs and Tradeoffs to Stakeholders

Potential costs and tradeoffs of this implementation would be that it adds workload to the students, TA's, and instructor. It would take a lot of time to both create the quizzes so that they are an accurate representation of what occurred in class that day, as well as actually taking the quizzes. This could increase the stress of the stakeholders and lead to more overall displeasure with the course. However, I think the overall perception that quizzes are effective and the drop in understanding when the class pace is too high suggest that the benefits of daily reinforcement quizzes ultimately outweigh the potential negative effects to the instructor, TA's, and students.
